title: Invariant affine generic neighbourhood with a finite locally free thickening
statement: Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Assume $s,t:R\to U$ are finite and of finite presentation [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and assume $U$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $u_1,\ldots,u_m\in U$, with $m\geq0$, have orbits $O(u)=t(s^{-1}(\{u\}))$ consisting of generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $U$. Then there exist an open subscheme $V\subseteq U$ and a closed subscheme $V'\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion] such that: $V$ and $V'$ are affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; $u_1,\ldots,u_m\in |V'|$; $s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)$; $V'\hookrightarrow V$ is a thickening of finite presentation, meaning a closed immersion of finite presentation inducing a homeomorphism on underlying spaces; and $s^{-1}(V')=t^{-1}(V')$ as closed subschemes of $R_V=s^{-1}(V)$. In particular the restriction groupoid with objects $V'$ and arrows $R'=V'\times_{U,s}R\times_{t,U}V'$ has source and target $s',t':R'\to V'$ finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tag 0ABC (lemma-invariant-affine-open-around-generic-point), statement; R-invariant subscheme has equal source and target inverse images.

proof.text: If $m=0$, take $V=V\prime=\varnothing=\operatorname{Spec}(0)$; all assertions are vacuous and the empty closed immersion is an isomorphism. Hence assume $m>0$. Choose $Z_n$ from [lem-sfb-finite-presented-groupoid-rank-filtration], and put $D_r=Z_{r-1}\setminus Z_r$. Every point lies in exactly one $|D_r|$. For a selected $u_j\in D_r$, invariance of each $Z_n$ implies that the entire orbit $O(u_j)$ lies in $D_r$: for an arrow with source $u_j$, membership of its target in each $Z_n$ equals membership of its source. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], each $O(u_j)$ is finite. Write $F=\bigcup_jO(u_j)$ and let $K$ be the finite set of ranks $r$ attained by $F$.

source.place: Tag 0ABC, first paragraph; Tag 0ABB, rank filtration and generic orbits

proof.text: For $r\in K$, let $E_r=\operatorname{int}_U(|D_r|)$. Every point $x\in F\cap D_r$ lies in $E_r$: apply [lem-sfb-generic-point-fp-closed-interior] to $Z_{r-1}\hookrightarrow U$ and intersect its resulting neighbourhood with $U\setminus|Z_r|$. Define $H(E)=U\setminus t(s^{-1}(U\setminus E))$ for an open $E$. This is open because $t$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]; it is invariant by [lem-sfb-groupoid-subset-saturation-invariant] and taking complements. The identity section gives $H(E)\subseteq E$. Inversion shows that $x\in H(E)$ if and only if $O(x)\subseteq E$: an incoming arrow from outside $E$ is inverted to an outgoing arrow to outside $E$. Thus $W_r=H(E_r)$ contains every selected orbit lying in $D_r$. The opens $W_r$ are pairwise disjoint since $W_r\subseteq |D_r|$.

source.place: Tags 0ABB and 0ABC, generic points in rank strata; invariant shrinking of those neighbourhoods

proof.text: Put $W=\bigcup_{r\in K}W_r$ and define $W\prime\hookrightarrow W$ on the disjoint open pieces by $W\prime_r=Z_{r-1}\times_U W_r$. These closed subschemes glue by their ideal sheaves, with no overlap conditions on disjoint pieces. Each has support $W_r$, hence $W\prime\hookrightarrow W$ is a homeomorphism. Invariance holds scheme-theoretically: the pullbacks of $Z_{r-1}$ agree and those of $W_r$ agree, so the pullbacks of their intersection agree on each common inverse-image open piece. By [lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal], the ideals of $Z_{r-1}$ are locally finitely generated. Their restrictions define $W\prime_r$, so the ideal of $W\prime$ is locally finitely generated too. Applying the same criterion makes $W\prime\hookrightarrow W$ of finite presentation. This constructs the required invariant thickening before imposing affineness; it contains $F$.

source.place: Tag 0ABC, reduction to a finitely presented invariant thickening; Tag 0ABB, finite presentation of its ideal

proof.text: On the open subscheme $W\prime_r\subseteq D_r$, the source is the open restriction of the finite locally free rank-$r$ map supplied in step 1. Indeed for an invariant monomorphism $T\to U$, the double restriction $T\times_{U,s}R\times_{t,U}T$ equals the single inverse image $R\times_{s,U}T$: the second membership condition is automatic by equality of inverse-image subschemes, and its lift is unique by the monomorphism. The source over $W\prime$ is therefore finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). Flatness and local finite presentation hold locally on the disjoint pieces, since open restriction leaves the relevant stalk maps and local affine presentations unchanged. Thus the source is finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Inversion interchanges source and target, so the target is likewise finite locally free. Denote this restricted groupoid by $(X,Q,a,b)$, with $X=W\prime$. On any affine chart the ideal of $W\prime$ in $W$ consists of nilpotents, because its vanishing set is all of that chart. Its pullback ideal is again nil, since a finite sum of multiples of nilpotent elements is nilpotent. Thus the closed pullback $Q\to R_W$ is a homeomorphism, and its source and target point maps identify the orbits in $X$ with the original orbits in $W$.

source.place: Tag 0ABC, replacement of the original groupoid by its restriction to the thickening

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is quasi-separated. To check this explicitly, take affine opens of $U$ contained in $W$ covering $W$, and pull them back through the closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow W$. These pullbacks are affine by the quotient-ring description of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The ambient affine opens have quasi-compact pairwise intersections by [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc]. Intersecting those intersections with $X$ preserves quasi-compactness: cover an intersection by finitely many affine opens, whose closed pullbacks are affine. The affine-cover criterion [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](2) proves the claim. The homeomorphism $|X|=|W|$ identifies every point of $F$ with a component generic point of $X$, since $W$ is open in $U$. Apply [lemma-nagata-affine-neighbourhood-generic-points-exists] with any point of the nonempty $F$ and the distinct generic points comprising $F$. Obtain one affine open $A\subseteq X$ containing $F$.

source.place: Tag 0ABC, final paragraph: a common affine open containing the finite union of generic orbits, Properties Tags 01ZV/01ZX

proof.text: On $X$ use the operation $H$ of step 2 with $(a,b)$ in place of $(s,t)$, and put $B=H(A)$. The same closed-image, saturation and inversion argument applies because $a,b$ are finite. It gives an invariant open $B\subseteq A$ containing $F$: each selected $u_j$ has its whole orbit in $A$, hence lies in $B$, and invariance then puts its entire orbit in $B$. Write $A=\operatorname{Spec}C$. Let $J\subseteq C$ be the ideal generated by the elements $h$ with $D_A(h)\subseteq B$. For every $x\in F$ the basic-open basis [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i) gives such an $h$ nonzero at $x$. Thus $J$ is not contained in any of the finitely many primes $\mathfrak p_x$, and [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] supplies $f\in J$ outside all of them. Consequently $F\subseteq D_A(f)\subseteq B$: a prime outside $B$ contains every generator of $J$ and hence contains $f$.

source.place: Tag 0ABC, final application of Groupoids Tag 03JE; its invariant interior and finite prime avoidance work for the whole finite union of orbits

proof.text: Set $V\prime=H(D_A(f))$. Step 2 gives an invariant open containing $F$ and contained in $D_A(f)$. Inversion exchanges $b(a^{-1}(X\setminus D_A(f)))$ and $a(b^{-1}(X\setminus D_A(f)))$. Hence $|V\prime|=B\cap\bigl(X\setminus a(b^{-1}(X\setminus D_A(f)))\bigr)$. Also $a^{-1}(B)\subseteq b^{-1}(A)$ because $B$ is invariant and lies in $A$. Apply [lem-pd-descent-norm-locus-affine] with its object scheme $X$, affine open $A$, intermediate open $B$, section $f$ and output $V\prime$. Its remaining hypotheses are $D_A(f)\subseteq B$, $V\prime\subseteq D_A(f)$ and finite, flat, locally finitely presented $a$, all proved above. The lemma gives affineness of $V\prime$. This is the norm argument for all the selected orbits together, without assuming that a union of separately constructed invariant affine opens is affine.

source.place: Tag 0ABC, final paragraph; Groupoids Tag 03JE, final norm argument

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq W$ be the unique open corresponding to $V\prime\subseteq W\prime=X$ under the homeomorphism $|W\prime|\to|W|$. Then $V\prime=V\times_W W\prime$ as schemes, since both are the open restriction of $W\prime$ to that set. Restricting the defining ideal of $W\prime$ gives a closed immersion $V\prime\hookrightarrow V$ with the same underlying points. The ideal is still locally finitely generated, so [lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal] gives finite presentation. By [lem-sc-closed-affine-union-affine] with the single affine closed subscheme $V\prime$, the scheme $V$ is affine. The set invariance of $V\prime$ in $X$ implies invariance of $V$ in $U$: for $r\in R$ over $W$, use the homeomorphism $|Q|=|R_W|$ established in step 4 and the equality of the two pullbacks of $W\prime$. Thus membership of $s(r)$ in $V$ equals membership of $t(r)$ in $V$. Equal open subsets give equal open subschemes. Scheme-theoretic invariance of $V\prime$ follows by restricting the equal pullbacks of $W\prime$ to this common inverse-image open, where it is exactly invariance of $V\prime$ in $X$.

source.place: Tag 0ABC, first paragraph, lifting the invariant affine open across the thickening and applying Limits Tag 09NL

proof.text: The points $u_j$ lie in $V\prime$ by construction. Its arrow scheme is $V\prime\times_{U,s}R\times_{t,U}V\prime$, as required. Since $V\prime$ is an invariant open in $X$, its source is the open restriction of $a$; finiteness is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), while flatness and local finite presentation are unchanged on these open restrictions. By [def-pc-finite-locally-free] it is finite locally free; inversion gives the same assertion for the target. This verifies every stated clause.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0ABC proof, using the invariant rank filtration and generic-interior argument of Tag 0ABB directly; finite-orbit version of the norm construction of Groupoids Tag 03JE

The item statement matches Stacks 0ABC (more-groupoids.tex 2582-2616) hypothesis by hypothesis and is not weakened. New node rank-filtration: this is 0AB9 plus the first sentence of the 0ABB proof. Finite presentation of the Fitting strata Z_r follows from 05P8 because s_*O_R is finitely presented. Z_0=U because O_U to s_*O_R is split by e^*. It is a true strengthening of the existing 0AB9 node, which has no finite-presentation conclusion, so it is not a duplicate and not a clause of the item. New node generic-fp-closed-interior: this is 0AAW(1) applied with Chevalley 054K. I checked the affine case: a finitely generated I inside a minimal prime p is nilpotent in A_p, so one denominator s gives D(s) inside V(I). It is true, the claim is about underlying sets only, and I found no duplicate in the DAG. Steps 1-9 all hold. Every point lies in exactly one D_r, and orbits stay in one D_r and are finite. Interiors and the invariant open H(E) are justified by t being closed, the saturation-invariance node and inversion. The glued thickening W' to W has support W_r inside Z_{r-1}, is scheme-theoretically invariant, and is of finite presentation by 01TV used in both directions. The restricted groupoid's source is the open restriction of the rank-r map, so it is finite locally free. X is quasi-separated, and the Nagata/01ZV lemma applies with x in F and distinct components. Prime avoidance (F nonempty) gives f with F inside D(f) inside B. All hypotheses of the 03JE norm lemma hold with s=a, t=b, W=B, giving V' affine. The open V is affine by 09NL, its invariance comes from |Q|=|R_W|, and the restricted arrows are finite locally free. Edge cases checked: m=0, repeated points, the trivial groupoid, unbounded ranks, non-Noetherian and non-reduced U. No hypothesis is missing.
